question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[2{X}^{2}-5].$

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{3},\,0<x<3
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[2{X}^{2}-5]=2\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-5
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the second raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}\,|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=3$ into the simplified expression, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2{X}^{2}-5] & =2\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-5 \\  & =2\cdot 3-5 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
